This story completely misses the Voat. The complaint here is not that electric cars harm the environment more than gas cars -- it is that the generation of electricity does. This is a critical distinction as electricity can be the end product of just about any power generation, whereas fossil fuel by definition cannot. Further, this end product, when obtained efficiently, will make cars far more efficient in energy consumption.

It doesn't help that this "National Bureau of Economic Research" is run by a former George W. Bush official.

It's totally possible that Internal Combustion Engine efficiency will surpass legacy power generation systems efficiency at some point. The idea that we should keep legacy power systems around is incredibly shortsighted, and as power generation and distribution continue to migrate closer to the customer with localized power generation (solar mainly) electric cars will have a much higher potential efficiency than Internal Combustion Engines could ever have (2nd law of thermal dynamics and all.)

if you drew a line graph of efficiency it would have a line that is tending towards the maximum efficiency for ICE and a line going to the upward right that goes all the way to Fusion power generation that dwarfs the ICE engine efficiency many times over (and ultimately theoretical battery/supercapacitor charge cycle efficiency maximums.)

Federal Court upholds Campaign Finance Ban and threatens Citizens United

This is an interesting read.

It wasn't even close on the voat (see what I did there?) either, 11-0 in favor of the constitutionality of the ban.

This decision alone will not topple Citizens United, but it is a good first step.

As much as I despise Citizens United I see very little here that isn't visible without rose colored glasses. This is an appellate decision that affirms the status quo, that government contractors can be forced not to participate in open lobbying efforts. (there are less direct methods that are still open to them) It's a good thing that the most basic of common sense can still be considered in force, however preventing a company from lobbying the government entities that they are contracted with is the lowest of fruits on the tree.

This theory that the Citzens United case somehow forced politicians to raise and spend billions and billions of dollars is a bit misguided. Politicians are able to raise so much money is because an individual politicians patronage is so valuable to those that are in a position to direct and control massive contributions. Politicians - and their enablers - will always find ways to use campaign finance rules to help themselves and their allies and to harm their opponents.

The only way to get too much money out of politices is somehow make it so that politicians don't control the distribution of too much money.
